claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine whether you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you tell me the **names and ages of the children** you're inquiring about? This will help me assess your eligibility on a per-child basis.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I'm looking to claim Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I have the basics about Alex, who is 8 years old.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to gather a bit more information about your circumstances.

**Are you responsible for Alex's care and do you live with Alex in the same household?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, Alex doesn't actually live with me at the moment, but I do help support him financially.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's important information.

To help me understand the situation better, **could you tell me more about why Alex doesn't live with you? For example, is Alex living with their other parent, a grandparent, or someone else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives with his other parent - my ex-partner.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for explaining that. That's helpful context.

**Do you have legal responsibility for Alex, such as through a formal custody arrangement, court order, or parental responsibility agreement?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm his parent, so yes, I have parental responsibility for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. That's useful information.

Now, to complete my assessment, I need to understand the living arrangements a bit more clearly.

**Even though Alex lives with your ex-partner, do you have Alex living with you for any part of the week or year - for example, on certain days, weekends, or during school holidays?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex lives with his mum full-time. He doesn't stay with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification. That's important for determining eligibility.

One more question to complete my assessment:

**Are you a UK resident, and do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on the information you've provided, I need to inform you that **you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex** under the current UK rules.

The key reason is that Child Benefit is paid to the person who is **responsible for and living with the child**. Although you have parental responsibility for Alex and provide financial support, Alex lives full-time with his mother (your ex-partner) and does not live with you.

Child Benefit is typically claimed by the person in whose household the child resides. Since Alex is living full-time with his mother, she would be the person who could claim Child Benefit for him, provided she meets the other eligibility criteria.
